calls.reason: The Nobel background says Hinton and colleagues 'reinvented' back-propagation, which supports the priority point. But the press release credits the Boltzmann machine and names predecessors, which undercuts his reading of the citation.
The AlphaFold paper and the Nobel release do not settle whether AlphaFold's search and constraint parts count as symbolic AI. No earlier Nobel was checked against that definition.

2024 evidence backs each part: Anthropic on opacity, Nature on hallucinations, the Alice-in-Wonderland tests on simple errors, and Meta's 15T tokens and 39.3M GPU hours. Water evidence is thin, but the main point holds.

This is a sweeping negative with no reliability threshold. Papers reporting 97–99% classification accuracy cut against it, but they do not show robust reliability in deployment, so it cannot be called either way.
